mainEntity.name: Do I need court permission before taking defensive driving for a ticket?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Contact the court named on your citation before enrolling for ticket dismissal. The court, not TexDDS, decides eligibility, court costs, deadlines, and which completion documents it will accept.

mainEntity.name: How long is the Texas defensive driving course?

acceptedAnswer.text: The licensed Texas driving safety course is six hours. TexDDS offers its ticket-dismissal course online, subject to court approval for dismissal.

mainEntity.name: How much does the TexDDS online defensive driving course cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The TexDDS online defensive driving course is $25 flat. There is no separate $3 materials or administration fee and no electronic delivery fee. Driver-record and insurance-course options are priced separately.

mainEntity.name: Can I take the course on a phone, and is there a final exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: TexDDS describes the online course as video-based and mobile-friendly for phones, tablets, and desktop computers. The course does not have a final exam.

mainEntity.name: What happens after I finish the course?

acceptedAnswer.text: Follow the TexDDS completion steps, then submit the certificate and any other required documents exactly as your court or insurer directs. TexDDS does not add an electronic delivery fee; the receiving court or insurer controls its own deadline and submission format.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a Type 3A Texas driver record?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many courts require one, but follow the instructions from the court named on your citation. Texas DPS identifies Type 3A as the driver-record type used for defensive driving.

mainEntity.name: What is included in the course and driver-record bundle?

acceptedAnswer.text: The $44.95 bundle combines the $25 defensive driving course with Type 3A driver-record ordering support. The record option is $5 less in the bundle than the $24.95 standalone record service.

mainEntity.name: Can I take defensive driving for an insurance discount?

acceptedAnswer.text: TexDDS offers a separate six-hour, $15 insurance-discount course. Ask your insurer whether it qualifies before enrolling. That option is not a ticket-dismissal course unless a court has separately approved your case and directed you to an eligible course.

mainEntity.name: Is Texas Defensive Driving School licensed by Texas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation lists Texas Defensive Driving School as a current Driving Safety Provider under license CP411. Directory inclusion verifies license status and is not a TDLR endorsement.

mainEntity.name: Is TexDDS online statewide, and are classroom courses available?

acceptedAnswer.text: The online course serves eligible drivers across Texas. TexDDS also offers scheduled or appointment-based in-person classes at its San Angelo classroom; call ahead for the next available date.
